conviction_note: The evidence points both ways and nets out. Q3 should show a GAAP swing to profit on the crypto rally (BTC +43%, ETH +71%) and the $40M buyback supports a stock trading near available capital per share. Against that, by my inference from the H1 fee table, Q3 management fees are flat because the 250bps XBT platform is shrinking in mix, and the Nov 18 call will speak into a ~20-25% Q4-to-date crypto drawdown. p_up is 49 on a 9% absolute move (a 68% realised-vol name with two prior reactions of -7.2% and +9.8%), so the scaled number is about -0.2, close to the -0.4 sum of the findings.
bar: Revenue: $31.47M for Q3 2026 from FXEmpire only (https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/cshr/earnings), basis unclear (GAAP revenue vs revenue-and-gains). EPS: $0.13 (FXEmpire) and $0.14 (TipRanks, 1 analyst; https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/CSHR/earnings), which roughly agree. There is no company guidance. The revenue bar has a single source, so every finding that depends on it is capped small. My GAAP revenue estimate is about $22-25M (management fees $16-18M plus staking, lending and other), built from the H1 MD&A fee rates and AUM by platform. That is about -15% to -30% against $31.47M if that figure is GAAP revenue, and in line or a beat if it includes capital-markets gains. Net income: my central estimate is about $18M ± 10M (≈$0.13 ± 0.07/share, ~138M shares), in line with $0.13-0.14.
positioning_check: Short interest is low: about 0.7% of shares, 907,881 shares short, days to cover 2.6 at the 2026-05-29 settlement (https://equibles.com/stocks/cshr/short-interest, via search snippet; the page itself timed out). An older 2026-04-30 snapshot showed 403.8K shares, DTC 1.0 (https://www.optionsanalysissuite.com/stocks/cshr/short-interest). I found no newer settlement. There is no usable option chain (baseline options.status empty_chain), so there is no skew. Tape: spot $3.38, -9.4% over 5 days, -14.4% over 20 days, -60.7% from the 52-week high, 1.5% above the 52-week low, about $1.1M a day of turnover. This is not a crowded short, so no squeeze mechanism. The drawdown matches the mid-November crypto selloff (BTC fell to roughly $62-69k on Nov 13-15 from about $84k at Sep 30).

findings.finding: Q3 2026 GAAP results should swing to a profit because of crypto marks. BTC rose ~43% and ETH ~71% in Q3 (BTC ~$58.5k to ~$84k). The H1 loss of $23.9M included a $15.4M loss on treasury BTC/ETH/SOL and a $16.6M XBT Pricing Differential loss. Both lines moved with prices: the differential was +$18.1M in H1 2025 when BTC rose and -$16.6M in H1 2026 when BTC fell 31.8%. So Q3 likely carries a treasury gain of roughly +$8-12M (ETH alone was $16.6M when sold in early October) and probably a differential gain. That supports GAAP EPS in line with or above the $0.13-0.14 consensus, against Q2's -$0.14 that drew a -7.2% reaction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 2026 (Sep 14) GAAP loss driven by these same marks plus listing costs: EPS -0.14 vs 0.10 forecast, stock -7.16% ($5.17 to $4.80). FY2025 print (May 1): EPS 0.10 in line, +9.84%. Source: https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/CSHR/earnings
findings.why_not_priced: Crypto prices are public, so the direction is partly priced. But one or two analysts cover the name, and if the marks were in the consensus EPS, it would sit well above $0.14 on a quarter with ~$12M segment EBITDA plus $10-25M of marks. Both line items sit below or outside segment EBITDA, so the market may look through them, which is why this is sized as a fraction of operating profit.
findings.independence: Q3 crypto returns from a different source: https://cryptobriefing.com/bitcoin-q3-up-44-best-quarter/ (BTC +44%) and https://forklog.com/en/bitcoin-posts-best-third-quarter-since-2017/ (+42.7%). The treasury sale sizes come from the Oct 27 6-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002087587/000119312526432650/cshr-ex99_1.htm

findings.finding: Q3 management fees are likely flat versus the H1 run-rate of $20.0M a quarter even though AUM is back to ~$7.4B, because of fee mix. The H1 MD&A gives XBT Provider at 250bps, now only 25% of AUM ($1.387B at Jun 30, net outflows $104.6M in H1). Physical is 15-150bps, Block 32.5bps and US 25-185bps. Applying those rates to Q3 average AUM by platform gives about $16-18M of management fees and about $22-25M of GAAP revenue. The single-source revenue consensus is $31.47M (FXEmpire). If that is GAAP revenue, Q3 misses it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On H1 (Sep 14) revenue fell 35.7% y/y to $51.4M and management fees fell 32.9%; the stock fell 7.16%, though the GAAP loss led the headlines. There is no clean history of a revenue-only surprise.
findings.why_not_priced: The headline the market saw was AUM: '26Q3 AUM in line with 25Q4 level' in the Oct 27 buyback release, and ~$6.9B at end-August from the H1 call. A reader of headline AUM would expect fees back near the Q4 2025 run-rate (~$31M a quarter: FY25 fees $126.4M). A ~$31M revenue consensus suggests that read. If the mix effect were priced, the revenue bar would sit in the low-$20Ms.
findings.independence: AUM recovery: H1 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15576995001074688, AUM ~$6.9B at Aug 31) and the Oct 27 6-K. The fee-mix arithmetic rests only on the MD&A, so this is my inference, not a company statement. The bar has one source. Shares the MD&A document with finding 1.

findings.finding: The Nov 18 call will report into a sharp Q4-to-date crypto drawdown. BTC was ~$84k at Sep 30 and ~$62-69k on Nov 13-15 (more than -20% since late October), with $1.91B of spot-ETF outflows over Nov 5-13. Expect October/November AUM commentary well below the ~$7.4B Q3 level and marks on the remaining treasury (BTC, half the SOL) and the XBT differential reversing in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no formal guidance history. At H1 the CEO's positive Q3-to-date AUM commentary did not stop a -7.2% reaction to the GAAP loss.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: CSHR is -14.4% over 20 days and -9.4% over 5 days, at its 52-week low. What is not priced is the company's own number for October AUM and flows (its monthly tracker is behind a form I could not open). Sized small as macro-to-company transmission.

findings.finding: On Oct 27 the board approved a buyback of up to $40M, about 9% of the ~$455M market cap at $3.38. It is funded by selling the whole ETH treasury ($16.6M) and half the SOL ($2.7M) in early October, before the Q4 crypto drop. Spot $3.38 is about 1.08x the H1 available capital of $3.14 a share that the former CFO cited on the H1 call. The Q3 release and call will likely report the first repurchases and a Sep 30 available capital figure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The buyback announcement itself drew +5.3% pre-market on Oct 27 (https://www.tradingpedia.com/2026/10/27/coinshares-jumps-premarket-on-40m-buyback-plan/). The stock has since given that back and more.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorisation is public. Not visible yet: how much has been bought (no 6-K on repurchases found) and the Sep 30 available capital per share. If the market priced a floor at available capital, the stock would not be trading within ~8% of $3.14 a share while the operating business made ~$21.6M of H1 segment EBITDA. Financing check: the treasury sale buys back shares at about 1x capital and the H1 balance sheet shows no long-term debt, so this is not distress.
findings.independence: H1 call transcript, available capital ~$3.14/share and pro forma 138.1M shares: https://www.webull.com/news/15576995001074688 . Shares the Oct 27 6-K with finding 1's treasury figures.

H1 already carried $2.2M of Bastion staff bonuses under the Growth Incentive Plan plus $1.9M of exceptional expenses, so Q3 likely has more deal and integration costs in unallocated costs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no isolated history. The H1 one-off costs were part of the GAAP loss that drew -7.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: The completion is public but the cost is unquantified. A thin consensus may not model integration costs. Small.

findings.finding: The CFO changed on Oct 1, 2026: Matt Morris, Deputy CFO since August 2026 and an adviser since 2025, replaced Richard Nash, CFO since 2019. Q3 is Morris's first report as CFO.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and minor. A first report by a new CFO sometimes brings a reset of disclosure or reserves, but nothing points to one here.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no skew and no history, so the only directional statement is the tape: -14% over 20 days into a crypto selloff, at the 52-week low and near available capital per share. My findings are mixed (a Q3 mark-driven profit and buyback support against flat fees and a weak Q4-to-date) and do not clearly cut against the run-up, so p_up sits near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 2 (one-offs): the treasury and XBT-differential profit swing sits below or outside segment EBITDA, so it was cut from +0.8 to +0.5.
Lesson 6 (bar): the revenue consensus has one source (FXEmpire) and its basis is unclear, so the fee-mix finding was capped from -1.0 to -0.7.
Lesson 5 (macro proxy): the Q4-to-date crypto drawdown is transmission the company has not confirmed and is largely in the -14% run-up, so it went from -0.8 to -0.6.

Lesson 8 (thin coverage): abs_move_pct went from 8 to 9 (one or two analysts, ~$1.1M a day of turnover, 68% realised vol); p_up went from 48 to 49 because the negatives lean on a single-source bar and a public proxy.
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest checked at ~0.7% of shares, DTC 2.6 (May), so no squeeze adjustment was needed. The buyback, Bastion and CFO findings are left unchanged.
